source_text: EVANGELICA praecepta, fratres dilectissimi, nihil aliud sunt quam magisteria divina, fundamenta aedificandae spei, firmamenta corroborandae fidei, nutrimenta fovendi cordis, gubernacula dirigendi itineris, praesidia obtinendae salutis; quae, dum dociles credentium mentes in terris instruunt, ad coelestia regna perducunt. Multa et per Prophetas servos suos dici Deus voluit et audiri; sed quanto majora quae Filius loquitur, quae Dei sermo qui in Prophetis fuit propria voce testatur, non jam mandans ut paretur venienti via, sed ipse veniens, et viam nobis aperiens et ostendens; ut qui, in tenebris mortis errantes, improvidi et caeci prius fuimus, luce gratiae luminati, iter vitae duce et rectore Domino teneremus. Qui inter caetera salutaria sua monita et praecepta divina quibus populo suo consulit ad salutem, etiam orandi ipse formam dedit, ipse quid precaremur monuit et instruxit. Qui fecit vivere, docuit et orare, benignitate ea scilicet qua et caetera dare et conferre dignatus est; ut, dum prece et oratione quam Filius docuit apud Patrem loquimur, facilius audiamur. Jam praedixerat horam venire quando veri adoratores adorarent Patrem in spiritu et veritate, et implevit quod ante promisit; ut qui spiritum et veritatem de ejus sanctificatione percepimus, de traditione quoque ejus vere et spiritaliter adoremus. Quae enim potest esse magis spiritalis oratio quam quae a Christo nobis data est, a quo nobis et Spiritus sanctus missus est? Quae vera magis apud Patrem precatio quam quae a Filio, qui est Veritas, de ejus ore prolata est? ut aliter orare quam docuit non ignorantia sola sit, sed et culpa, quando ipse posuerit et dixerit: Rejicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem vestram statuatis. Oremus itaque, fratres dilectissimi, sicut magister Deus docuit. Amica et familiaris oratio est Deum de suo rogare, ad aures ejus ascendere Christi oratione. Agnoscat Pater Filii sui verba cum precem facimus. Qui habitat intus in pectore, ipse sit et in voce. Et cum ipsum habeamus apud Patrem advocatum pro peccatis nostris, quando peccatores pro delictis nostris petimus, advocati nostri verba promamus. Nam, cum dicat quia quodcumque petierimus a Patre in nomine ejus dabit nobis,, quanto efficacius impetramus quod petimus in Christi nomine, si petamus ipsius oratione?
pass_a_gloss: The evangelical teachings, most beloved brothers, are nothing other than divine instructions, foundations for building hope, reinforcements for strengthening faith, nourishments for fostering the heart, guiding principles for directing our journey, and strongholds for obtaining salvation; which, while instructing the docile minds of believers on earth, lead them to the heavenly kingdoms. God wanted to be called and heard by many through the prophets, His servants; but how much greater are the things that the Son speaks, which the Word of God, who was in the prophets, testifies with His own voice, no longer commanding that a way be prepared for Him to come, but coming Himself, and opening and showing us the way; so that we, who previously wandered in the darkness of death, imprudent and blind, might hold the path of life, enlightened by the light of grace, with the Lord as our guide and director. Among other salutary admonitions and divine teachings by which He consults His people for their salvation, He also gave the form of prayer Himself, and instructed and taught us what to pray for. He who made us live also taught us to pray, with that benignity by which He deigned to give and confer other things upon us; so that, while we speak to the Father with the prayer and supplication that the Son taught us, we may be more easily heard. He had already predicted that the hour would come when true worshipers would worship the Father in spirit and truth, and He fulfilled what He had previously promised; so that we, who have perceived the spirit and truth of His sanctification, may also worship Him truly and spiritually, according to His tradition. For what prayer can be more spiritual than the one given to us by Christ, from whom the Holy Spirit was also sent to us? What prayer can be more true before the Father than the one spoken by the Son, who is the Truth? So that to pray otherwise than He taught is not only ignorance, but also fault, when He Himself said and established: You reject the commandment of God, to establish your own tradition. Let us pray, therefore, most beloved brothers, as God, our teacher, taught us. It is a friendly and familiar prayer to ask God for what is His, and to ascend to His ears with the prayer of Christ. Let the Father recognize the words of His Son when we make our prayer. He who dwells within our breast should also be in our voice. And when we have Him as our advocate with the Father for our sins, and we ask as sinners for forgiveness for our offenses, let us pronounce the words of our advocate. For when He says that whatever we ask of the Father in His name, He will give us, how much more effectively do we obtain what we ask for in the name of Christ, if we ask with His own prayer?
